sampling: Body paragraphs (blank-line blocks after front matter, headings excluded; tables, code, lists, images count as blocks; 214 total). Started at paragraph 3 and took every third (3, 6, 9, ... 213); 15 claims chosen from the sampled blocks spread across the post, 8 of them numeric.

score_evidence.A: Coherent problem -> mechanism -> internals -> install -> usage -> config -> deploy -> metrics -> choice arc; no body H1, no skipped levels, 20 balanced fences, $$-only math, use_math true, two-level categories, no author key, description 122 chars opening with 'vLLM'. Deductions: L27 orphan one-sentence paragraph ('어림 계산으로 옮기면, 40GB의 약 30%인 12GB 남짓이 ...'); L244 empty-ish table cell '—'; L752 H2 is a 60-character sentence-length heading.
score_evidence.B: Mostly natural '입니다' prose. Deductions: L509 broken sentence '이 남은 공간을에서 본 고정 크기 물리 블록으로 잘라 풀을 만듭니다' (-> '이 남은 공간을 앞에서 본 고정 크기 물리 블록으로 잘라 풀을 만듭니다'); L23 '행렬-벡터 곱을 하나씩 수행하므로' (-> '행렬-벡터 곱을 하나씩 계산하므로'); L652 '각 줄은 서로 다른 역할을 맡습니다' (-> '줄마다 하는 일이 다릅니다'); L237 formulaic '규칙은 한 문장으로 줄어듭니다'; L133 one sentence carries a full English article title plus series name; 11 '할 수 있습니다'.
score_evidence.C: Deductions: L694 '앞서 소개한 premai.io의 비교 글' - premai is never introduced earlier; running-example context length drifts: L544 sets '--max-model-len 8k' for the tuned chat server, but L674 says '앞서 정한 컨텍스트 길이' and uses 2048 (taken from the deliberately extreme OOM example at L586); the Runpod article is called 'Runpod의 vLLM 해설 글' (L294), '서드파티 글 "vLLM Explained"' (L782) and then '"vLLM Explained"가 인용한 Runpod의 서드파티 비교' (L786), as if two sources; TL;DR facts re-stated in body (L13 vs L19 'UC Berkeley에서 개발한 오픈소스').
score_evidence.D: Hard parts get worked examples at the right time: 7-token/block-4 allocation (L86-101), slot_mapping vs block_table table (L137-142), CoW ref-count table (L179-183), beam-search block tables (L203-217), local/remote prefix-hit arithmetic (L362-368). Minor over-explanation: the 1000/16=63 waste calculation is done twice (L103 and L519-521).
score_evidence.E: Tables, block-table text diagram, EngineCore diagram and figures are placed where discussed and referred to descriptively. Deductions: L760 embeds only perf_a100_n3 (n=3) yet L762 compares 'n=1일 때와 병렬 출력이 3개일 때' as if both were shown, and the caption omits n=3; animations hotlinked from vllm.ai (L148, L193).
score_evidence.F: Deductions: L703/L706/L710/L735/L750 build the metrics section on 'vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc', which current vLLM no longer exports (loggers.py and docs/design/metrics.md: 'vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc'); the name comes from a vLLM forum thread (-2). L682-684 YAML nests modelRevision under vllmConfig while the chart template reads $modelSpec.modelRevision, so the pin advised at L688 is silently ignored (-1; the docs page's own bullet list nests it ambiguously). L139-140/L144 say prefill reads no block_table ('해당 없음 (일반 셀프 어텐션)'), which is the paper-era V0 behaviour, inside a section about V1 slot_mapping; V1 chunked prefill/prefix caching read paged KV during prefill (-0.5). L279 excerpt 'self.kv_cache_manager.free(request)' is stale vs current '_free_request_blocks' (labelled abridged; minor). All 14 other sampled claims supported.
score_evidence.T1: Install (uv venv/--torch-backend=auto/vllm download-kernels), LLM/SamplingParams, llm.chat, vllm serve with engine flags, curl chat request, CompilationConfig/CompilationMode, tensor_parallel_size=2, docker run all match current docs and would run as pasted. Two defects a reader hits: the /metrics grep will not show a KV-cache line on current vLLM, and the Helm modelRevision pin has no effect.
score_evidence.T2: Covers the sources' important topics in a sensible order (paper mechanisms, V1 blog, quickstart, install, engine args, conserving memory, Docker, Helm). Padding: L772-773 third-party benchmark rows from low-authority 2026 blogs (buildmvpfast, iotdigitaltwinplm) and L742-750 GuideLLM issue thread detail.
score_evidence.T3: Strong internals (block table, CoW, beam search, gang-scheduled preemption, V1 EngineCore, hash-based prefix caching, KVConnector lookup), integration (Helm, metrics, scaling limits) and choice/failure-mode closing. Commands and defaults follow current docs; design advice reads as recommendation ('편이 낫습니다'). Minor: L499 leans on the v0.9.2 docs page for '--help' advice.

examples.source: Paper §1: '13B-parameter LLM on an NVIDIA A100 GPU with 40GB RAM. Approximately 65% ... model weights ... Close to 30% of the memory is used to store the dynamic states' (12GB is the post's own arithmetic, labelled 어림 계산).

examples.claim: 기존 시스템은 KV 캐시 메모리의 20.4%~38.2%만 실제 토큰 상태에 사용; 낭비 4% 미만
examples.source: Paper §1: 'only 20.4% - 38.2% of the KV cache memory is used to store the actual token states'; vLLM blog: 'a mere waste of under 4%'.

examples.claim: TP에서도 KV 캐시 매니저 하나; 워커는 같은 물리 블록 ID를 쓰되 자기 헤드의 KV만 저장
examples.source: Paper §4.6: 'vLLM features a single KV cache manager within the centralized scheduler ... Although each GPU worker has the same physical block IDs, a worker only stores a portion of the KV cache for its corresponding attention heads.'

examples.claim: CoW table: blocks 7,1 ref count 2; A1 write -> new block 3, copy, block 1 count to 1; A2 writes directly
examples.source: Paper §4.4: 'the reference counts for physical blocks 7 and 1 are both 2 ... allocates a new physical block (block 3), instructs the block engine to copy ... decreases the reference count to 1. Next, when sample A2 writes to physical block 1, the reference count is already reduced to 1'.

examples.claim: Beam search k=4: blocks 2,4,5,8 freed; new blocks 9-12; all share 0,1,3; 0&1 share 6; 2&3 share 7
examples.source: Paper §4.4: 'vLLM frees all physical blocks whose reference counts reach 0 (blocks 2, 4, 5, 8) ... allocates new physical blocks (blocks 9-12) ... all candidates share blocks 0, 1, 3; candidates 0 and 1 share block 6, and candidates 2 and 3 further share block 7.' (Pre-iteration table L203-208 is reverse-derived and says so.)

examples.claim: Swap overhead high at small blocks; recompute constant; blocks 16~64 comparable end-to-end
examples.source: Paper §7.3: 'recomputation overhead remains constant across different block sizes ... For medium block sizes from 16 to 64, the two methods exhibit comparable end-to-end performance.'

examples.claim: V1 up to 1.7x throughput vs V0 (without multi-step scheduling); ShareGPT, Llama 3.1 8B / Llama 3.3 70B; larger for Qwen2-VL on VisionArena
examples.source: V1 blog: 'delivering up to 1.7x higher throughput compared to V0 (without multi-step scheduling)'; 'Llama 3.1 8B and Llama 3.3 70B models using the ShareGPT dataset'; 'testing Qwen2-VL using the VisionArena dataset. V1 delivered even larger speedups'.

examples.claim: --prefix-caching-hash-algo choices sha256/sha256_cbor/xxhash/xxhash_cbor, default sha256; xxhash needs optional package; collision risk in multi-tenant
examples.source: Engine Args: 'Possible choices: sha256, sha256_cbor, xxhash, xxhash_cbor ... Requires the optional xxhash package ... leak private information in multi-tenant environments ... Default: sha256'.

examples.claim: GPU guide adds --managed-python; --torch-backend=auto or UV_TORCH_BACKEND=auto; --torch-backend=cu126; uv self update if it fails
examples.source: GPU install: 'uv venv --python 3.12 --seed --managed-python'; 'If this doesn't work, try running uv self update'; Quickstart: 'To select a specific backend (e.g., cu126), set --torch-backend=cu126'.

examples.claim: --api-key or VLLM_API_KEY; multiple keys after --api-key accepted, useful for rotation
examples.source: Quickstart: 'You can pass multiple keys after --api-key, and the server will accept any of the keys passed, this can be useful for key rotation.'

examples.claim: --kv-cache-memory-bytes: per-GPU KV size in bytes, default None, ignores gpu_memory_utilization when set
examples.source: Engine Args: 'Size of KV Cache per GPU in bytes. By default, this is set to None ... kv_cache_memory_bytes (when not-None) ignores gpu_memory_utilization'.

examples.claim: vllm serve ... --max-model-len 8k --block-size 16 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --enable-chunked-prefill --kv-cache-dtype fp8 are valid engine args
examples.source: Engine Args: --max-model-len 'supports k/m/g/K/M/G ... 1k -> 1000'; --block-size, --max-num-seqs, --max-num-batched-tokens, --enable-chunked-prefill present; --kv-cache-dtype 'CUDA 11.8+ supports fp8 (=fp8_e4m3)'. Note 8k = 8000, not 8192.

examples.claim: values-02-basic-config.yaml keys table (requestGPU, pvcStorage, replicaCount/requestCPU/requestMemory, repository/tag/modelURL, vllmConfig sub-keys, modelRevision, env)
examples.source: Helm Chart Deployment page 'Explanation of Key Items' lists exactly these keys with matching meanings. (Placement of modelRevision in the L684 YAML is a runnability defect, see extras.runnable_code.)

examples.claim: /metrics exposes KV cache usage as vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc alongside vllm:num_requests_running/waiting
examples.source: Current vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py registers 'vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc' (no gpu_cache_usage_perc); docs/design/metrics.md: '`vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc` (Gauge) - Fraction of used KV cache blocks'. The post's name comes from the vLLM forum thread it cites.

examples.claim: vLLM blog: n=1 HF 14~24x, TGI 2.2~2.5x; n=3 HF 8.5~15x, TGI 3.3~3.5x; A100/A10G
examples.source: vLLM blog: 'vLLM achieves 14x - 24x higher throughput than HF and 2.2x - 2.5x higher throughput than TGI ... three parallel output completions ... 8.5x - 15x ... 3.3x - 3.5x'; 'LLaMA-7B on an NVIDIA A10G GPU and LLaMA-13B on an NVIDIA A100 GPU (40GB)'.
